identification.name: Nylon 6 (PA6)
identification.common_form_notes: Widely stocked as extruded rod, sheet, and plate for machining (gears, bushings, wear pads). Also available as FDM filament, though less common than PA12/nylon-composite blends for printing — nylon filament is especially hygroscopic and must be dried immediately before printing (and stored in a sealed container with desiccant), since absorbed moisture causes poor layer adhesion and visible steam/popping at the nozzle.
identification.notes: Values are for the general-purpose (unreinforced, unfilled) grade, primarily from MatWeb's aggregate "Overview of materials for Nylon 6, Unreinforced" page, which averages across hundreds of specific commercial datasheets (grade counts noted below) — more statistically representative for a general/typical entry than any single manufacturer's datasheet. Grade counts behind the stored values: Young's modulus n=465, yield strength n=458, tensile strength n=323, elongation n=626, density n=816, shear strength n=8, compressive yield n=17, specific heat n=42, melting point n=604, max service temperature n=108, glass transition n=5, Poisson's ratio n=7, Shore D hardness n=46. Nylon is strongly hygroscopic — the stored tensile strength (67.0 MPa) is an average across moisture states and sits between AZoM's single moisture-conditioned datasheet value (40 MPa) and the nylonplastic.com comparison guide's dry-as-molded figure (~80 MPa); real parts absorb ambient moisture in service, so use the low end of this range for conservative design margins. MatWeb's aggregate also reported a Thermal Conductivity average of 2.89 W/m·K (n=64) — disregarded as implausible for an unreinforced thermoplastic (typical nylon k is ~0.2–0.3 W/m·K; the source's own stated range tops out at 31.7 W/m·K, a metal-like figure that suggests contamination from filled/reinforced grades despite the "Unreinforced" filter, or a data-entry error in the aggregated dataset); left null rather than propagate it. Shear strength is a directly-reported value, not derived. Electrical conductivity is nominally 0% IACS (International Annealed Copper Standard) — i.e. an electrical insulator.

typical_usage: Gears, bushings, bearings, rollers, wear plates, cable ties, and general-purpose machined or moulded parts needing a tough, low-friction, wear-resistant plastic. A common substitute for POM/Delrin where slightly better toughness and lower cost matter more than POM's superior dimensional stability and lower moisture sensitivity.
